edits.what: mirrored WS_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 'mekstation.v1', WS_CREDENTIAL_PREFIX = 'mekstation.token.', toBase64Url() and credentialProtocols() from src/lib/multiplayer/socketCredentialProtocol.ts
edits.why: bare-node ESM with no TypeScript loader cannot import the .ts module — the same constraint that forced the server.js mirror
server.js:855-863 refuses a URL-borne credential outright (reason=token-in-url) since #1357

edits.what: `new WebSocket(url, { perMessageDeflate: false })` -> `new WebSocket(url, credentialProtocols(wireToken), { perMessageDeflate: false })`
edits.why: supplies the credential through Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, matching src/lib/multiplayer/client.ts:690-693

the independent robustness defect — replayPromise's error timer is armed first and fires first, so a handshake failure rejected it with no handler attached, killing the process and skipping both finally blocks

assertions: declares the same subprotocol names as the module — constant parity against the imported WS_PROTOCOL_VERSION / WS_CREDENTIAL_PREFIX, not retyped literals

encodes the credential byte-identically to the module — lifts the validator's own toBase64Url body out of the source with a regex, makes it callable via new Function, and compares its OUTPUT to the module's across 7 fixtures exercising '+', '/', one and two trailing '=' pads, and a realistic base64-of-JSON wire token. Behavioural, not textual, because a transform drift presents as a 401 rather than the 400 this file was written for.

offers the credential on the subprotocol, not in the socket URL — `expect(source).not.toMatch(/[?&]token=/)` and `not.toMatch(/token=\$\{/)`, plus a positive check that `new WebSocket(url, credentialProtocols(wireToken)` is present. Deliberately does NOT trip on the SessionJoin payload's `token: wireToken` property, which is a different carrier and must keep working.
keeps a pre-await replay rejection observable — asserts `replayPromise.catch(() => {});` is present
